dedupe_keys.name: nova scotia drillhole database dp me 3

description: The Nova Scotia Drillhole Database records 28,341 drillholes in the province with more than 40,000 references to the reports that document their drilling and later work; 6,597 of the holes have core stored at the provincial Core Library in Stellarton. It is compiled by the Nova Scotia Department of Natural Resources and Renewables from mineral exploration assessment reports, open file reports and Geological Survey of Canada publications. Coverage is the province of Nova Scotia; version 6 was released in 2023. The data come as one ZIP file of 36 MB, 426 MB unpacked, holding ESRI shapefiles, an ArcGIS file geodatabase, Google Earth files and Excel sheets, in UTM zone 20 on NAD83, free under the Nova Scotia Open Government Licence. Caveats: holes come from reports of many decades, so locations and depths vary in accuracy, and the database indexes holes and references, not full logs. For simulation it gives subsurface information for mineral potential studies and for ground conditions along planned roads, pipelines and foundations, and for hazard exposure work on old mine workings. It is related to the OpenGeoSys and GemPy records in this catalogue, which model subsurface processes and geology from such drillhole data.
